end.summary:
- Reviewed the East India Company’s change from trader to ruler, 1600–1858.
- Zoya sequenced the Charter (1600), Plassey (1757), Buxar (1764), Diwani rights and Crown rule (1858) correctly without help.
- Practised forts, armies, alliances, battles and revenue rights as methods of gaining power.
- Explained effects on shopkeepers, weavers, Dhaka, taxation and Company finances.
- No misconceptions recorded; teach-back was not completed because Zoya felt tired and hungry.
end.parentNote: Zoya practised the timeline from the 1600 Charter to Crown rule in 1858 and explained how forts, armies, battles, alliances and Diwani rights helped the Company gain power. She also described how cheap machine-made cloth affected local shopkeepers and weavers, including Dhaka. She mixed up the exact Buxar participants once, but this was not revisited later in the lesson. At home, ask her to retell the timeline using four points: Charter, Plassey, Buxar and Crown rule.
